description: CONVOLUTION as a GRAPH-NATIVE, sense-agnostic perceptual primitive — no Python. A kernel is graph data (a Kernel node's `weights`), a sensory FIELD is graph data (a Field with Patch nodes, each a flattened window), and a convolution RESPONSE is the DSL Term MaxOver(field's patches, Dot(kernel.weights, patch.vals)) evaluated in Rust. The same primitive applies to ANY sense: a cochleagram window (hearing), an image patch (vision), any projected field. The kernel FAMILY (onset/offset/edge/centre-surround/diagonal/smoother) is seed data the agent designs; a sense KEEPS the kernels that discriminate (effect-gate). The convolution lives in the graph + Rust DSL; Python only lays the field patches (I/O ingest) and reads responses.

microtheory.name: sensory_convolution
microtheory.description: convolution = MaxOver(patches, Dot(kernel, patch)); kernels are graph data; sense-agnostic.

attrs.discrimination_comment: GRAPH-NATIVE discrimination over a Sense's labelled fields: (mean between-label dist - mean within-label dist) / (between + within), scale-normalised. dist(f1,f2) = Sum over kept_kernel of (conv_resp(f1,k)-conv_resp(f2,k))^2. A Rust DSL fold; no Python math.

rules.name: keep_discriminative_kernel
rules.comment: GRAPH-NATIVE effect-gate: a sense (considers the ConvFaculty, has_field its labelled fields) KEEPS a kernel whose response SPREAD across the fields exceeds 0.1x the most-varying kernel's spread. spread(k)=MaxOver(fields, conv_resp)-MinOver(fields, conv_resp); conv_resp=MaxOver(patches, Dot(kernel.weights, patch.vals)). The KEEP decision is this Rule (Rust-evaluated), not Python; the world only provides the fields (affordances).
